title: A Asset for the Border
premise: Ivo Okonkwo, a hostage negotiator whose one public failure still defines him, is quietly hired to handle a hijacking that officially never happened: every record of Flight 447 vanishes mid-flight, along with the passengers' identities. As he traces the erased manifest across three countries, he realizes the flight carried a defector holding proof of a coordinated data purge—and that his own name has been scrubbed from the negotiator registry to keep him deniable. Hunted by an assassin who only kills people who no longer exist, Ivo must smuggle the truth through border checkpoints, burned safehouses, and a final negotiation where the hostage is the evidence itself. He ends the failure on his board by trading his own invisibility for the passengers' restoration, walking into custody as the world learns Flight 447 landed.
about_author: Rosalind Underhill is a former customs analyst who spent a decade documenting what crosses borders and what never gets recorded. She writes thrillers about paper trails, quiet disappearances, and the people caught between jurisdictions.

chapters.title: The Unattributed Call
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A fixer offers him a job so sensitive it can't be logged: talk down a man barricaded in a cargo office at a regional airport. Ivo succeeds, but notices the airport's systems show no inbound flights that night. Emotional beat: professional pride shadowed by the suspicion he's being used as a ghost.

chapters.title: One Failure Still on the Board
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Flashback woven into present: the Marseilles negotiation that ended in three deaths and made him unemployable in official channels. His handler, Vera Lindqvist, warns him the new case is 'unattributable.' Emotional beat: grief recast as expertise—he is hired precisely because he knows how to be forgotten.

chapters.title: Flight 447
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The barricaded man was a ground controller who watched Flight 447 land with no transponder, no filing, no passengers disembarking—then was ordered to forget it. Ivo pulls the radar archive; the track exists for eleven minutes, then nothing. Emotional beat: vertigo—the first crack in a reality he trusted.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Isn't
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He finds the booking records: 212 seats sold, then refunded simultaneously at 40,000 feet. One passenger, Amara Diallo, never took her refund. Her last message: 'They will say we were never on it.' Emotional beat: the dead becoming visible through a single anomaly.

chapters.title: Vera's Ledger
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Vera discovers Ivo's own credentials have been quietly purged from the negotiator registry—someone is pre-erasing him. She keeps a private ledger of every unattributable job she's brokered, and four entries now share a client code. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling into fear for the man she placed in harm's way.

chapters.title: Border Crossing, No Stamp
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Following Diallo's trail to a border town, Ivo finds his own passport flags no entry history anywhere—a man without a paper past. He meets a retired customs officer who remembers the flight landing and cargo containers leaving under diplomatic seal. Emotional beat: belonging stripped away; identity revealed as paperwork.

chapters.title: The Man Who Kills Ghosts
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV (unnamed). We meet the killer, contracted to erase everyone connected to Flight 447—including a negotiator whose file just went blank. He studies Ivo's photo and finds it oddly familiar. Emotional beat: cold professionalism disturbed by a flicker of recognition.

chapters.title: Amara's Suitcase
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. In Diallo's storage unit: a hard drive containing the defector's proof—a coordinated purge of flight records across three governments, run by a private consortium selling 'historical discretion.' Emotional beat: purpose crystallizing; the failure on his board reframes as practice for this.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Denial
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo approaches a journalist and a sympathetic aviation regulator; both are dead within thirty-six hours, their deaths ruled unrelated accidents. He understands the rules: anyone who acknowledges the flight becomes erasable. Emotional beat: isolation deepening into resolve.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Vera shelters Ivo and calculates their odds aloud like a negotiation: two assets, one drive, three borders. She reveals the client code traces to a consortium board member who once sat on the panel that reviewed the Marseilles failure. Emotional beat: the personal and political cases fusing into one.

chapters.title: Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Smuggling the drive across a land border inside a child's toy donated to a refugee family—an act of trust with strangers who don't know they're couriers. The assassin watches from the queue and lets them pass, wanting Ivo to lead him to the buyer. Emotional beat: fragile hope built on ordinary decency.

chapters.title: What the Assassin Remembers
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV. The killer interrogates a consortium courier and recognizes the technique used to keep him compliant years ago: memory work, the same program that produced him. He was made from erased people. Emotional beat: the hunter discovering he is also cargo.

chapters.title: The Registry Room
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo breaks into the consortium's records annex and finds the master list of everything ever disappeared—including his Marseilles operation, altered to guarantee its failure. His defining wound was manufactured. Emotional beat: rage and release; the failure was never his.

chapters.title: Burn Notice, Reverse
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Vera burns her ledger selectively, feeding fragments to three embassies so no single government can bury the story alone. She knows this ends her career. Emotional beat: sacrifice as strategy; making herself attributable to save Ivo.

chapters.title: Negotiation with No Hostage
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Cornered in a freight yard, Ivo does what he does best: negotiates—with the assassin, offering him the proof of his own origins in exchange for passage. The assassin hesitates for the first time in his career. Emotional beat: empathy as weapon; seeing the enemy as a casualty.

chapters.title: The Landing They Denied
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo locates the hangar where Flight 447's actual fuselage sits, disassembled, alongside crates of seized belongings—212 lives reduced to evidence. He photographs everything and uploads copies to dead-man servers. Emotional beat: mourning made concrete; names restored to objects.

chapters.title: Three Borders in One Night
chapters.summary: Ivo and assassin's alternating POV. A running chase across checkpoints, the assassin now clearing paths instead of closing them, both men hunted by the consortium's cleanup teams. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance forged in motion; trust as a live transaction.

chapters.title: The Buyer's Table
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo walks into the consortium board member's office and opens negotiations for the only thing he wants: full restoration of the manifest, the passengers' names, and his own file—in exchange for silence about the buyer's identity. Emotional beat: the negotiator finally negotiating for himself.

chapters.title: Terms of Existence
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The board member counters: take money, stay invisible forever. Ivo refuses—visibility is the ransom. The assassin arrives as leverage, tipping the deal toward publication. Emotional beat: climax of identity; choosing to exist over surviving unseen.

chapters.title: Flight 447 Lands
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The story breaks simultaneously in three capitals: the manifest published, the fuselage photographed, the consortium exposed. Families learn their people were real. The assassin disappears into the crowd, carrying his own file. Emotional beat: catharsis; the erased stepping back into the light.

chapters.title: Attribution
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo surrenders to authorities to face the reopened Marseilles inquiry—now with evidence it was sabotaged. Vera testifies. For the first time, his name appears in an official record he chose. Emotional beat: accountability reclaimed as belonging.

chapters.title: A Asset for the Border
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, epilogue. Cleared but changed, Ivo takes a post training border negotiators, teaching them that every person is a record someone might try to delete. He keeps Amara Diallo's unsent refund notice framed above his desk. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; memory as the border worth defending.
